verdicts.title: Make ctypes endianness reversal pure: compute reversed bytes from a snapshot, never mutate the caller's object
verdicts.issues: RESOLVED by orchestrator revision: elem_size==0 early-return guard added to the Array branch, preserving the old b"" result for zero-sized-element arrays. Original issue: One fix-introduced regression, otherwise verified end-to-end. REGRESSION: the Array branch of _reversed_ctype_bytes computes elem_size = ctypes.sizeof(elem_type) and then iterates range(0, len(raw), elem_size); for an array whose ELEMENT type has sizeof 0 (e.g. class Empty(Structure): _fields_ = []; (Empty * 3)()), elem_size is 0 and range(0, 0, 0) raises 'ValueError: range() arg 3 must not be zero'. The OLD code serialized this shape fine (returned b'' -- reproduced on the pristine repo), so this is a crash caused by the patch, contradicting the 'correct for shapes the old code crashed on' framing. One-line fix: guard the Array branch with 'if elem_size == 0 or not raw: return raw' (or equivalent) before the range loop. Everything else checks out empirically on the patched copy (Windows, little-endian host): before-snippets are verbatim against bytemaker/conversions/ctypes_.py lines 44-71/96-99/148-152; all 10 claimed repro behaviors reproduce exactly (caller non-mutation for struct/array-of-struct/aggregate, nested-struct 010200000a0b0c0d, struct+array-field 1122aabbccddeeff, array-of-u16 now actually reversed, union passthrough, native no-op, bytes_to_ctype big); adversarial shapes all pass: nonzero padding bytes preserved at correct offsets (mixed u8/u32), _pack_=1, trailing padding, arrays-of-arrays, zero-length arrays of nonzero-size elements (incl. as struct field -- old code raised IndexError there, new works), c_char arrays and c_char-array struct fields (chars not byte-swapped), 3-deep nesting, struct-containing-union (union bytes passthrough at nested level, other fields reversed), union-containing-struct (top-level passthrough), _anonymous_ union and struct fields, c_bool/c_char/c_wchar/c_float/c_double, c_void_p and c_char_p struct fields (reversed, matching old behavior), POINTER(...) struct fields (passthrough; old code raised AssertionError), BigEndianStructure/LittleEndianStructure round-trip with per-field reversal of stored bytes; error paths: undersized/oversized bytes_to_ctype raise/behave identically to old (same ValueError text), and the nested-bitfield error path no longer corrupts the caller (old code left it partially reversed). Derived-struct-inheriting-base-fields output is bit-identical to old (base fields untouched) as the risk note claims. reverse_bytes_unit: grep over the whole repo (incl. tests, .pyi, __init__ exports) finds no references outside ctypes_.py and findings/observations docs -- deletion is safe. Oracle lockstep verified: _legacy_aggregate.py lines 23-29 import ctype_to_bytes/bytes_to_ctype/ctype_to_bits/bits_to_ctype from bytemaker.conversions.ctypes_ (no duplicated copy); legacy to_bytes_aggregate on the patched copy no longer mutates the ctypes field; full suite 854 passed on the patched copy (test dir copied beside patched package, module __file__ confirmed), plan_fastpath_test.py + aggregate_types_test.py re-run separately: 204 passed. Docstring style matches the module's existing Google-style Args/Returns sections. Minor nits (no action forced): POINTER fields pass through while c_void_p fields are byte-reversed -- asymmetric but matches old c_void_p behavior and pointers are nonsensical to reverse anyway; the Array branch derives element count from len(raw) rather than the type's _length_, benign on all in-repo call paths (verified oversized-input behavior identical to old); dropped '# type: ignore' markers may matter if mypy/pyright is run over the file.

verdicts.title: Check every _fields_ entry (including nested structures') for bitfields and name the offending field in the error
verdicts.issues: Verified empirically on the patched copy; all claims hold and the guard is stronger than claimed. Before-snippet is verbatim (lines 54-63). BitFirst (bitfield first) -> NotImplementedError naming field 'a'; BitLater (bitfield later) -> NotImplementedError naming field 'b' (old code: ValueError: too many values to unpack, reproduced on pristine); BitNested -> NotImplementedError with dotted path 'bf.a' (old code: TypeError after PARTIALLY CORRUPTING the caller -- new code leaves caller bit-identical, verified); bitfields inside an array of structs -> NotImplementedError with path 'arr[0].a' (old code: TypeError); decode direction via bytes_to_ctype raises the same clean error; native-order direction still serializes bitfield structs unchanged (no reversal attempted). The check-before-unpack ordering is correct (len(field) tested before field descriptor/offset use), and because the guard only writes to a local bytearray, no partial state escapes on raise. Caveats correctly disclosed in the solution: bitfields inside Unions are NOT rejected (union passthrough policy -- deliberately congruent with ctypes-1's decision item, for the maintainer to rule on), and the solution is not separable from ctypes-1 (it lives inside _reversed_ctype_bytes) -- the offered standalone fallback (any(len(f) > 2 ...)) is accurately scoped. Note: this shares the ctypes-1 implementation, so the zero-sized-element Array regression flagged under ctypes-1 technically lives in the same function, but it is not a guard defect; fix it once under ctypes-1.

verdicts.title: Fix run-together words in the ctype_to_bytes / bytes_to_ctype TypeError messages
verdicts.issues: Verified. Before-snippets verbatim (lines 90-94 and 142-146, including the '# type: ignore'). On the patched copy: ctype_to_bytes(123) -> '... _SimpleCData, Structure, Union, and Array objects, not <class ''int''>.' and bytes_to_ctype(b'\x00'*4, int) -> '... types, not <class ''int''>.' -- both spaces restored (pristine repo reproduces the run-together 'Structure,Union'). Third cited site (lines 57-62, the garbled 'arenot supported.Ctype instance: ...' NotImplementedError) is deleted wholesale by ctypes-2 and its replacement message is well-formed and names the offending field by dotted path -- confirmed no residue of the old string remains and coverage of the 57-62 portion of the ux ref is real. Existing tests test_invalid_ctype_to_bytes/test_invalid_bytes_to_ctype assert only the exception type (confirmed by reading test/ctypes_test.py lines 63-70) and keep passing; no code matches on these strings (grep). Full suite 854 passed with all three fixes applied together.
